newsitem.title: USA: Detroit to sell $15 mln TIF bonds in coming months.
newsitem.headline: Detroit to sell $15 mln TIF bonds in coming months.

text.p: - Detroit Finance Director Valerie Johnson said late Wednesday that the city expects to issue $15 million of tax increment financing bonds for new professional sports stadiums in the next month.

Johnson also said the city is considering a financing based an the collection of delinquent taxes. She estimated that there was more than $100 million in delinquent property taxes to collect, but noted that Detroit's collection rate is improving and the actual figure will be significantly less.

Detroit is not considering a bulk sale and would earmark the money for specific projects, Johnson said. Because the city has a budget surplus, it would not be used for closing a gap in the budget, she added.
Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer made collecting delinquent income taxes a main focus of his state-of-the-city address earlier this year.

The financing for the new $500 million football and baseball facilities for the Detroit Lions and Detroit Tigers respectively also includes $80 million of bonds closed on Tuesday from the joint Detroit and Wayne County stadium authority.
